lensA_claim_1.claim: Invariant 1 is violated because `ls daedalus` shows gates+kernel+spine side by side.
lensA_claim_1.why: Coexistence is not the measurement, and the measurement does not support 'three competing kernels'. spine and kernel are not parallel planes: 76 of 146 entrypoints reach BOTH under the file-level closure, 21 under the strict import-time closure, and 34 under the invocation closure - i.e. they are layers on one call path, not rival control planes. gates is not a control plane at all: ZERO effect-boundary registry rows target it, and it is reached by exactly one entrypoint in all three modes, its own `python -m daedalus.gates report`, which builds a report and prints JSON.
lensA_claim_1.narrowed_residue: What IS measurable: only 5/35 gates modules and 14/23 kernel modules are reachable from any entrypoint, and 101/285 package modules are reachable from NO entrypoint at all. That is a dead-weight / test-only-surface question, not an Invariant-1 violation.

lensA_claim_2.claim: promote_candidates takes no approval parameter (and so never reaches kernel/approvals.py).
lensA_claim_2.why: At TRUNK the sealed callable takes 4 approval-shaped parameters (consumed_approval, evidence_packet, approval_ledger, owner_keyring), refuses fail-closed when approval_ledger/owner_keyring are missing, and reaches daedalus.kernel.approvals in 2 hops via daedalus.kernel.promotion, whose authorize_persisted_promotion is annotated with ApprovalLedger and ConsumedOwnerApproval. At CHECKPOINT the same function has 0 approval-shaped parameters and daedalus.kernel does not exist. Lens A's sentence is a true statement about the CHECKPOINT tree (and about the retired legacy body still retained as _gated_writes_legacy.py.src, which gated_writes.py deletes at import), read onto the TRUNK tree where it is false.
